first_response.first_response: Timestamp of first issue comment authored by a human who is not the reporter (excludes accountType=app and bot-like display names).
first_response.not_used: Assignee change alone is NOT counted as first response (tracked separately in closer/worker section).
first_response.hour_slas: Highest ≤2h, High ≤6h — elapsed calendar hours created→first_response.
first_response.day_slas: Medium ≤2 / Low ≤4 / Lowest ≤6 business days (IST dates, Mon–Fri; no holiday calendar).

resolution.closed_at: First changelog transition into a terminal status (not resolutiondate).
resolution.highest: Met if same IST business day (busday_count==0) OR ≤24 calendar hours (continuous-effort proxy).
resolution.low: Met if ≤10 IST business days (~2 weeks).
resolution.lowest: No committed resolution SLA — excluded from meet rate.

ops.closed_definition: current status in ['ACCEPTED', 'Approved', 'Approved - Assigned to Backlog', 'Approved - Fast Track Project', 'Awaiting Deployment', 'Canceled', 'Cancelled', 'Completed', 'DECLINED', 'Declined', 'Done', 'ENHANCEMENT', 'Failed']
ops.ttr_and_closer: first changelog status transition into a terminal status (not Jira resolutiondate — 185 issues share resolutiondate 2026-06-16)
ops.ttr_unit: elapsed calendar hours (created → first terminal status)
ops.weekly: ISO week in IST of first terminal status transition; grouped by changelog author
ops.mismatch_heuristic: flag when closer != top non-reporter commenter and that commenter has >= 2 comments

notes: Closed-at = first changelog transition to terminal status (not resolutiondate).
Business days = IST Mon–Fri; no company holiday calendar.
Case types from summary/description rule classifier.

wfi.definition: Sum of hours spent in status 'Waiting for Input' from changelog intervals (open interval ends at now if still in WFI).

definition.closer: Author of first changelog transition to terminal status.
definition.top_commenter: Non-reporter human with most comments on the ticket.
definition.mismatch: closer != top_commenter AND top_commenter has ≥2 comments.

narrative_bullets: Across 395 May–Jul PES tickets, comment/summary mining highlights **missing data / no rows** (128), **config / mapping change** (113), and **vendor delay / upstream** (100) as the dominant textual pain signals.
22 tickets (5.6%) mention a GitHub PR in comments — useful proxy for 'needed a code change' vs pure rerun/config.
Infra pressure themes (CPU/memory/disk/node) and vendor/upstream language show up enough to treat capacity and vendor SLAs as first-class runbook tracks, not one-offs.
Handoff/urgency language in comments correlates with closer≠worker mismatches — process debt, not just tech debt.

privacy.note: Person names anonymized for public GitHub Pages. Ticket summaries redacted. Aggregates unchanged.
